newsitem.title: USA: Former CIA chiefs see U.S.-China conflict threat.
newsitem.headline: Former CIA chiefs see U.S.-China conflict threat.

text.p: Two former CIA directors said on Thursday there is a danger of a military clash between the United States and China in the Taiwan Straits if they do not handle their differences carefully.

"For the next several years, I believe that the Taiwan Straits will be the spot in the world in which the clash of two major powers -- the United States and China -- is the most likely," former Central Intelligence Agency head James Woolsey told the House of Representatives National Security Committee.
He said he believed the focus of Chinese nationalism would turn to Taiwan after China takes over Hong Kong this summer.

"China would be foolish to consider an invasion of Taiwan for the foreseeable future," Woolsey said. "But seizure of one or more of the offshore islands or ballistic missile threats against Taiwan are real possibilities."

He said the United States was less likely to get into a war with China than with North Korea, Iran or Iraq but the greatest possibility of a major power conflict will be between the United States and China.
Former CIA Director James Schlesinger told the panel the U.S.-China confrontation last March in the Taiwan Straits showed the danger of war there.

"We drifted into the crisis in the Taiwan Straits," he said. "It was largely a reflection of misunderstandings on both sides but it raises the problem of whether or not these misunderstandings might lead to a serious military confrontation."

Schlesinger did not elaborate. The United States sent two aircraft carriers into the straits after China launched missile tests and manoeuvres near Taiwan, which Beijing considers a renegade province.
Woolsey was President Bill Clinton's first CIA director. Schlesinger was a director under President Richard Nixon.
